amazon.task: buy a physical product on Amazon: search for an item, work the results list, open and assess a product page (price, rating, variant options, delivery date), add to cart, and check out; complete when the order confirmation or the final checkout review screen with the order total is on screen. Surface pinned: Amazon's own website or app — not a third-party wrapper or assistive shopping app, not a haul/unboxing video, not a deals-roundup or affiliate-listicle without a live purchase session. Variants: returns and refunds (see returns), reordering a past purchase (see reorder), leaving a review (see review), and Amazon Fresh grocery orders (see groceries) do not belong.

questions.question: Should you continue with a truncated export of 1,000 listings, or close the dialog to refine your search?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether a truncated dataset is sufficient for your evaluation or if applying stricter filters is necessary to capture all relevant listings.

questions.question: Should you browse these broad search results or apply more filters to narrow them down?

questions.question: Did your new filter apply correctly, and how many properties remain?

banking.task: carry out an everyday banking task in a bank's own website or app (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Capital One, a credit union): sign in, then complete one concrete arc — transfer money between accounts, deposit a check with the camera, or find and download/read a statement — through the bank's review-and-confirm step; complete when the bank's confirmation of the transfer or deposit (or the opened statement) is on screen. Surface pinned: the bank's own app or site — not p2p apps (Venmo/Cash App belong to the p2p domain), not budgeting apps, not crypto exchanges.

tree.label: Manage the bank account
tree.note: do 1 then 2, then the job the session is for: 3 then 4 to send money - 3 runs standalone first when the recipient is new (22Zy, 2NVw) and collapses to the pick at 4.3 when saved (60Qk); 5 to put money in; 6 to pull a statement or receipt; 7 to open a deposit. no keeper runs more than two jobs: 48jl runs 5 twice for two methods, 7-fw runs 6 twice (receipt, then statement), 22Zy chains 3 into 4. then 8 - and 8 reaches into 6.10 and 6.11 when the success screen offers the receipt (4bGB, 5RS4). 22Zy takes its baseline for 8.3 before 1 even starts, on the receiving bank's own site.

children.label: Get into the bank
children.note: 1.1 where the app is not already at hand, then 1.2. 1.3 and 1.4 as the login asks; 1.5 to 1.7 on a first run - 7GBO answers five device prompts and passes a SIM gate before ever seeing an account, and two permission denials bounce it into unrelated flows it has to back out of.

questions.question: Do you accept the terms of the online banking service agreement?
questions.why: This matters because checking the box legally binds you to the rules, fees, and liabilities outlined in the Bank of America Online Banking Service Agreement shown on the screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent legally binds you to the bank's terms and conditions without you reviewing your personal rights and liabilities.

questions.question: Which app in this folder should you select to use a bank's own platform?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Finance' folder containing both P2P services like Venmo and traditional bank apps like Chase, requiring a choice that fits the strict task constraints.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the agent will correctly distinguish between a third-party payment service and their actual bank's official application.

questions.question: Do you want to log in using your fingerprint or enter your password manually?
questions.why: The screen displays a biometric prompt overlaying the password field, offering a choice between a quick fingerprint scan and manual password entry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to utilize their personal, physical biometric data for quick and secure authentication.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing highly sensitive banking credentials with a third-party agent, compromising account security.

questions.question: How do you want to receive your verification code?
questions.why: The bank requires an Advanced Access code for security, and you must select a delivery method like a text message to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which of their personal devices or contact methods receives the sensitive two-factor authentication code.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means sharing your highly sensitive debit card PIN and SMS authorization codes with a third-party agent.

calendly.task: land a meeting time with another person through a scheduling tool (Calendly, Doodle, Microsoft Bookings): open the invite link — or set up the event/poll and get it answered — compare availability, pick a slot, confirm; complete when the meeting-confirmed screen, or the poll's agreed final time, is on screen with the event details. Either side of the handshake belongs as long as the recording reaches a confirmed time. Surface pinned: a scheduling tool on the web. Variants: emailing back and forth about times, plain calendar-event creation with no counterparty, and configuring availability settings without a resulting booking do not belong.

questions.question: Where do you modify the scheduling settings for this specific event type?
questions.why: The screen showed the public booking page for the event, not the dashboard edit view as claimed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to properly configure their availability if the agent hallucinates the interface.

questions.question: Do you need to set buffer times or limit your daily bookings?
questions.why: The collapsed settings showed no buffer time and no maximum bookings, which could result in back-to-back meetings if left unadjusted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to enforce personal scheduling boundaries like breathing room between calls or a cap on daily meetings.

questions.question: Should you use your regular meeting hours or set custom availability for this specific meeting type?
questions.why: The screen presented a dropdown to choose between regular meeting hours and custom availability hours.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to dictate specific hours for this meeting type, which could result in unwanted bookings outside their preferred window.

questions.question: Should you adjust the default availability hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM?
questions.why: The screen displayed a default schedule of Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, which might not accurately reflect your actual working hours or preferences.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might blindly accept the default hours, potentially allowing others to book meetings at inconvenient times.

questions.question: Do you want your general availability to repeat weekly or be a one-time schedule?
questions.why: The screen provides a dropdown to choose whether your appointment availability repeats weekly or does not repeat.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might commit you to a recurring weekly schedule when you only wanted to offer one-time availability.

questions.question: How far into the future do you want to allow invitees to book?
questions.why: The screen displays the 'Date range' section under scheduling settings with options like 'calendar days into the future' and 'Indefinitely', which control your availability window.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strategically limit how far in advance meetings can be scheduled based on your upcoming workload or preferences.

questions.question: How much advance notice do you need before a meeting can be booked?
questions.why: The advanced options menu allows you to adjust the minimum lead time to prevent unexpected last-minute bookings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might leave the default one-hour lead time in place, exposing you to sudden meetings without adequate time to prepare.

questions.question: How do you want to adjust your availability for this specific date?
questions.why: The screen provides a link to change a date's availability, allowing you to override your default schedule for specific days.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might not account for personal, unrecorded commitments that affect your actual availability on that specific day.

questions.question: What buffer time is currently set for after the event?
questions.why: The 'Scheduling settings' page showed 'Buffer time: 15 min after' under 'Event limits', which dictates how soon another meeting can be booked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure they have adequate breathing room between scheduled meetings.

questions.question: How much buffer time do you want to add between appointment slots?
questions.why: The screen includes a checkbox to add time between appointment slots and a dropdown to specify the exact duration.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to customize your schedule's pacing, as an agent might just accept the default thirty-minute buffer or leave it disabled entirely.

questions.question: Which calendars do you want to check for conflicts, and what color should the schedule be?
questions.why: The screen provides options to select which calendars to check for availability and to customize the color of the appointment schedule.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify which calendars to check for conflicts and to personalize the schedule's color.

questions.question: What additional information should you require from the person booking the meeting?
questions.why: The booking form allows you to add custom required fields, which determines the specific context collected from attendees before the meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether asking for extra details like the meeting's purpose is worth the added friction for the invitee.

children.label: Pick the candidate slots

questions.question: What earliest and latest times should you offer for the meeting?

children.label: Publish the invitation

creditcard.task: apply for a credit card online as a consumer: open the card's apply page, fill the application (personal info, income, SSN-type identity fields), review disclosures and terms, submit, and see the decision or "under review" state; complete when the application-submitted or decision screen is on screen. Surface pinned: a bank or card issuer's website or app (Chase, Discover, Capital One, Amex, Citi, Bank of America). Variants: "best credit cards" rankings and reviews, credit-repair content, activating or using a card, and business payment-processing (merchant) content do not belong.

devicesetup.task: set up a new device through its companion app or on-device flow: a new phone (setup, account sign-in, data transfer), a router or mesh Wi-Fi via its app, a smartwatch pairing, or a smart-home device (camera, plug, speaker, doorbell): the unbox-to-working arc — pair or connect, sign in, configure the essentials; complete when the device shows working/connected in the app or the phone reaches its fully set-up home screen. Surface pinned: the setup flow itself — not unboxing-only or review videos.

tree.label: Set up a new device
tree.note: do 1, then 2. phone routes then do 3 and 4, where 4.3 is the whole of 4. accessory routes do 4 first, then 2.5 to 2.8, then 3 - the app will not look for a device until it knows the account. then 5 where anything is carried over; uSN0 and DT4C's first pass skip it outright. then 6. 7 always, and 7.9 when 7 comes back wrong. 8 on the transfer routes, reaching into 1.10 where the erase is actually run (aawv). 9 where the device has services to configure - fok5 and NZzD do parts of it inside 6, u--l does all of it after 7.

children.label: Prepare the devices
children.note: 1.1 to 1.3 on boxed hardware only (NZzD, u--l, fok5, 9yTg); 1.4 when the hardware will not enter setup mode (9yTg). 1.5 and 1.6 on the devices being replaced, in any order. 1.7 first on the new device, and 1.10 when the answer is wrong (mIjR, _CVz). 1.8 where a transfer will run long (aawv, CKwc). 1.9 where the route leans on a backup - CKwc and _CVz satisfy it by reading a timestamp instead of running one. 1.10 also serves goal 8: the same erase, at the other end of the task.

ebay.task: bid on an eBay auction as a buyer: find an auction listing, review item condition, seller rating, and shipping, place a bid by setting a maximum bid, confirm the bid, and see the resulting bid status; complete when the bid-confirmed state ("You're the highest bidder" or "You've been outbid") is on screen. Surface pinned: the eBay website or app. Variants: selling or listing items, dropshipping/reselling content, "Buy It Now" only purchases (that is ordinary shopping), and sniping-tool promotions do not belong.

tree.label: Win an eBay auction
tree.note: 1 where the account demands it - most keepers arrive signed in. 2 unless the listing is already at hand - ten keepers open on the target. then 3, then 4; T5mb runs 3.5 before anything else. 5 stages the bid - 5.2 replaces the bid box for the three accounts with no payment on file, and none of them ever bids. 6 owns the clock: snipers hold inside it, immediate bidders fall straight through to 6.6 (08WT, s_CE, B7Zu, fAtx). 7 whenever the outbid notice lands - it can interrupt 6 or follow it. 8 when the clock resolves; a loss ends there. 9 after a win, and 9.4 loops the whole task back to 2 - six times in Zkom. fx1m runs 5 and 6 across four windows at once.

email.task: compose and send an email in a mail client (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail, Apple Mail): open compose, address the recipient, write the subject and body, optionally attach a file, send it, and verify it in Sent; complete when the message shows as sent. Surface pinned: the mail client's compose-and-send flow — not inbox-organizing tours, not newsletter/marketing tools, not email-etiquette advice videos.

tree.label: Send an email
tree.note: 1 when the client is not already open and signed in - most keepers start authenticated and skip most of it. then 2: a new message, or a reply or forward entered from 8.1 (DFXu, ycKB, 6rzA, 0D7H, zCsj), which decides how much of 3 is left to do. 3 and 4 in either order - HnFK writes the subject and body before the recipient. 5 where the message carries a file; 5.4 only when the client refuses the file, and it returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready (UehN never gets back). then 6, one of 6.2 to 6.5; 6.6 and 6.7 where the client interrupts. then 7 - in this corpus that's where the task actually completes, and 7 is skipped by seven keepers. 8 at any point.

questions.question: What information should you enter into the recipient, subject, and body fields?
questions.why: The New Message screen contains blank fields that must be filled with the correct contact and message content to ensure the email reaches the right person and conveys your intent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over the exact wording, tone, and specific recipient of your communication.

children.note: 1.1 then 1.2. 1.3 only from a logged-out start - two keepers. 1.4 where more than one account is signed in. 1.5 and 1.6 as orientation before any composing, and only on the videos that tour the client.

questions.question: Which app do you open to access your email?
questions.why: The home screen displays multiple applications, so you must select the specific mail client you want to use to send the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific email client or account is used to send the message.

questions.question: How should you enter your sign-in credentials?
questions.why: The sign-in screen requires an email and password, which can be typed manually or autofilled using a password manager.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to securely autofill your credentials using a specific password manager or type them manually.

questions.question: Which email account are you currently sending from?
questions.why: Opening the profile pop-up reveals the active email address, '[email]', ensuring the message is sent from the correct account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify or switch their sender identity before composing the message.

questions.question: Do you need to verify your current email address before composing?
questions.why: Checking the profile pop-up confirms the exact email address and storage status you are currently using.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to confirm you are sending the email from the correct account.

children.label: Open a compose surface
children.note: 2.1 for a new message. 2.2 and 2.3 instead when the message answers one that arrived, entered from 8.1 - and that choice sets what 3 has left to do: reply-all arrives with To and Cc filled, forward arrives with To empty and quoted history attached. 2.4 after the draft exists. 2.5 where the compose surface is a panel that can be resized. 2.6 before typing, on the two keepers that tour the surface first.

questions.question: How do you forward this message to someone else?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Forward' link below the thread automatically populates a new compose window with the original message and a 'Fwd:' subject line.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to forward the existing thread or summarize the information in a brand new email.

questions.question: Should you change the response type to Reply, Reply All, or Forward?
questions.why: The screen shows a dropdown menu that lets you switch the current draft between a direct reply, a reply to all, or a forward.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually control exactly which participants from the original email thread will receive your message.

children.label: Set the recipients
children.note: 3.1 in nearly every keeper - typing resolved by a suggestion is close to universal here. 3.2 where the address is not in the list. 3.3 to reach the copy fields, then 3.4 and 3.5 where the message needs them. 3.6 replaces all of it on a bulk send, and rules 3.3 to 3.5 out. 3.7 whenever a chip is wrong. 3.8 before trusting a group. reply-all routes arrive with this goal already done (DFXu).

questions.question: Should you send this generic draft or use a different method to personalize the greeting for each recipient?
questions.why: The screen shows a single draft addressed to multiple recipients with a generic 'Hey' greeting, which prevents addressing each person by their actual name.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the personal touch of addressing each recipient by name, which makes the mass invitation feel less genuine.

questions.question: Which email address should you select as the recipient?
questions.why: The screen displays a list of multiple available email accounts, so you must select the correct one to ensure the message reaches the intended person.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong recipient from the list, potentially sending your message to an unintended contact.

questions.why: The screen shows multiple contact suggestions as you type the recipient's name, meaning you must click the correct one to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the personal oversight of ensuring your message isn't accidentally routed to a similarly named but incorrect contact.

questions.question: What exact email address are you entering in the 'To' field?
questions.why: Entering the precise email address in the 'To' field ensures the message reaches the correct person instead of bouncing or going to a stranger.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to personally verify that the recipient's address is typed perfectly to avoid sending the message to the wrong person.

questions.question: Who are you sending this email to, and what are the constraints for entering their address?
questions.why: The email address must be typed perfectly without any spaces or errors, otherwise the message will fail to reach the intended recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually verify the exact spelling and formatting of the recipient's address to ensure successful delivery.

questions.why: Revealing the Bcc field through the Options tab is necessary to keep the email addresses of all recipients private.

children.note: 3.6.2 first - the feature has to be switched on before anything else changes. then 3.6.1, and one of 3.6.3 or the pair 3.6.4 and 3.6.5. 3.6.6 is read after the fact in this keeper, not before.

questions.why: Clicking the mail merge icon revealed a dropdown to add recipients from a spreadsheet, which fundamentally changes how the email is addressed.

questions.why: The screen displayed a mail merge menu and a banner explaining that this feature lets you personalize messages with tags and sends a separate copy to each recipient.

flights.task: book a flight online (Google Flights, airline websites and apps, Expedia, Kayak): search a route and dates, compare fares and times, pick an outbound and return, enter passenger details, and reach the payment or confirmation step; complete when a booking confirmation or itinerary summary with the fare total is on screen. Surface pinned: a flight-booking site or airline app — not an airport kiosk, not a travel vlog, not a points/miles explainer without a live booking session. Variants: checking in for a flight (see checkin), researching and comparing without booking (see itinerary), and hotel or car add-ons after the flight is booked do not belong.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually browse the calendar and adjust your travel days based on personal flexibility.

questions.question: How many people are traveling, and what are their age categories?
questions.why: The screen provides specific age categories like adults, youths, children, and infants to calculate the correct fare and seat requirements.

questions.question: Which cabin class do you want to search for?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to set your baseline comfort level, potentially ending up with a restrictive Basic Economy ticket when you might have preferred to browse premium cabins.

questions.question: Should you include nearby airports in your search?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide if the inconvenience of traveling to an alternative nearby airport is worth the potential savings or better flight times.

questions.question: Should you restrict the search to direct flights only or include nearby airports?
questions.why: Checking the direct flights box prevents long layovers, while adding nearby airports might surface cheaper but less convenient routes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might prioritize a cheaper fare with a long layover over your preference for a faster, direct route.

questions.question: Are your search parameters correct and have you reviewed the site alerts before searching?

govbenefits.task: apply for a government benefit online or manage an existing claim (unemployment insurance, SNAP/food stamps, disability, Medicaid, housing assistance — state portals and agency sites): work through the eligibility screens and application form and submit, or certify/check an existing claim; complete when the submission confirmation or the claim-status screen is shown. Surface pinned: the government benefits portal itself — not benefit-explainer talking heads without a portal session.

tree.label: Claim a government benefit
tree.note: 1 then 2 every session. then the session's job: 3 once per claim, 4 every week the claim lives, 5 when certifying lapses, 8 once benefits flow onto the card. 6 closes 3, 4, and 5; 7 follows 6. the jobs chain across sessions - 3's confirmation starts the clock on 4, and 4 stays blocked while 5 processes (76Pa).

children.label: Reach the right program
children.note: 1.1 and 1.2 in either order; 1.3 and 1.4 before committing to the session - 1.4 can end it before it starts (iVa7's outage window). then 1.5. certifiers re-enter here every week.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify firsthand that your sensitive information is being submitted to the official government web address.

questions.question: Do you have a smartphone ready to take a picture of your ID and a selfie?
questions.why: The 'Before You Start' screen explicitly states that a smartphone is required to capture images of your ID and a selfie for identity verification.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An AI agent cannot physically use a smartphone to take a live selfie or photograph your physical ID card.

questions.question: Do you want to review the tips and document requirements before starting the application?
questions.why: The screen provides optional dropdowns with details on required documents and interview expectations that can help prepare you for the process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to learn exactly what documents to gather beforehand and what to expect during the interview phase.

questions.question: Which method will you choose to file your claim given the online system's restricted hours?
questions.why: The screen lists online, phone, and mail options, but specifies that the online portal is only open during certain days and times.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to choose an alternative filing method like phone or mail if the online system is currently unavailable.

questions.question: Have you noted the system's availability hours and upcoming downtime before continuing?
questions.why: The screen displays specific deadlines for weekly certifications and upcoming system downtime that could affect your ability to file on time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you might miss critical information about system outages and strict deadlines for your weekly certification.

questions.question: Which service portal should you select?
questions.why: The screen offers distinct portals for individuals, businesses, and government entities, so you must choose the one that matches your account type.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the agent is accessing the correct portal for your personal Social Security record.

questions.question: Which benefit program portal should I access?
questions.why: The screen displays different benefit systems like UI Online, so you must select the one that matches your specific claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the agent is entering the correct portal for your specific type of benefit.

children.label: Establish the account
children.note: 2.1 decides the wall: sign in (2.4), register (2.2, sometimes on the agency, sometimes on Login.gov or ID.me - the evidence notes say which), or guest past a CAPTCHA (q2an; 8v-j allows guest for one program only). 2.3 where the agency demands proofing - D3uH and o9iF are entire sessions inside this goal, and CA and AZ interpose it mid-application (a0_z, 5P67).

questions.question: Did your account creation succeed, and are you now viewing the main dashboard?
questions.why: Confirming the 'my Social Security' dashboard loads ensures your account was created properly and displays your initial eligibility and work credits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss seeing your immediate eligibility status, work credits summary, and any urgent unread messages upon first logging in.

questions.question: Is my account activation complete, and how do I proceed?
questions.why: Confirming the 'Congratulations!' message ensures your secure account is active before you click 'Next' to access the actual benefits portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the security guidelines and ensure your new login credentials are safely recorded before moving forward.

questions.question: Do you want to log in, create an account, or apply without an account?
questions.why: The login page provides options to enter existing credentials, create a new profile, or use the link to apply without an account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the choice of whether to link this application to a permanent account for easier tracking or to proceed immediately as a guest.

questions.question: Do you want to create an account to save your progress and get updates?
questions.why: The site recommends creating an account so you can save your application, receive alerts, check your status, and upload documents later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent continues without an account, you lose the ability to easily track your application status, receive automated updates, or resume the process later.

children.label: Register a new account
children.note: 2.2.1 then 2.2.2; 2.2.3 and 2.2.4 where the portal uses them; 2.2.5 where a confirmation email closes the loop; 2.2.6 wherever the form plants one. Or9Z fills everything and deliberately never submits - the narrator already has an account.

questions.question: What email, password, and security questions do you want to use to register your account?
questions.why: The registration page requires you to set up login credentials, four security questions, and a personal image with a caption to secure your new profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose memorable security answers and a personal caption that you can easily recall for future account recovery.

questions.question: Are you ready to submit this registration form?
questions.why: Clicking 'Next' officially submits the entered personal details to the government system to create a record.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to halt the process before a permanent, official government record is created with their personal data.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms and conditions required to establish an online account?
questions.why: The screen states that you must check the agreement box and click 'I Agree' to accept the Terms and Conditions in order to create your EDD account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review the specific legal terms and conditions you are binding yourself to by creating the account.

questions.question: Do you meet the strict age and residency prerequisites required by the Terms of Service to create this account?
questions.why: The Terms of Service explicitly state you must have a U.S. mailing address and be at least 18 years of age to legally proceed with account creation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally review the legal prerequisites and ensure they are not violating the Terms of Service by creating an account they are ineligible for.

questions.question: Can I use a shared email address for this account?
questions.why: The instructions explicitly state that you must use your own personal email address and not one shared with a spouse or family member.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might use a proxy email address, depriving you of direct, private access to critical communications regarding your benefits.

questions.question: What password will you create to meet the 12-character requirement and achieve a strong rating?
questions.why: The portal requires a password of at least 12 characters without common phrases and provides a real-time strength indicator to confirm it is acceptable.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose a personal, memorable password that you can easily recall for future access to your benefits account.

questions.question: What PIN hint question and answer should you choose to secure your new account?
questions.why: The registration screen requires selecting a PIN hint question and providing an answer so the system can securely assign your PIN and User Name.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent selects your security question and answer, which could prevent you from recovering your account if you forget your login details.

questions.question: Which personal image and caption should you select for your security check?
questions.why: The image and caption you choose will be displayed during future logins to confirm you are on the authentic EDD website before entering your password.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent selects these security features, you will not know the specific image and caption combination needed to verify the site's authenticity yourself.

questions.question: How do you confirm your email address to proceed with account creation?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Confirm email address' button in the Login.gov email is required to verify your address before the link expires in 24 hours.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires granting the agent access to your personal email inbox to click the confirmation link, which compromises your private communications.

questions.question: Which link should you click in the registration confirmation email to proceed?
questions.why: The email provides a direct 'Benefit Programs Online' link that safely routes you back to the official portal to log in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires granting the agent access to your personal email inbox to retrieve the continuation link.

questions.question: What characters do you need to enter from the CAPTCHA image?
questions.why: The 'Getting Started' page requires you to enter the exact text shown in the CAPTCHA image to verify you are human before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means relying on the agent's ability to accurately read and solve visual CAPTCHAs, which often block automated systems.

children.label: Prove the identity
children.note: 2.3.1 first where a provider fork exists; then 2.3.2 and 2.3.3. one of 2.3.4 or 2.3.5 proves the person - documents and a selfie (D3uH), or typed details against credit records (o9iF), or a bare typed SSN (VNaP, 5P67 - CA and OH ask for nothing more than that plus a license number). 2.3.6 and 2.3.7 where the agency stacks its own layer on top.

questions.question: Are you ready to verify your identity using your driver's license and Social Security number?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that a driver's license or state ID and your Social Security number are strictly required to prove your identity to the SSA.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires handing over highly sensitive physical identification documents and your Social Security number to a third-party agent.

questions.question: Which identity provider should you use to sign in or create your account?
questions.why: The portal requires choosing between third-party identity services like Login.gov or ID.me because the legacy Social Security username option is no longer available.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the opportunity to select the identity provider that best accommodates your specific residency status or existing account history.

questions.question: Do you want to use ID.me to verify your identity?
questions.why: The portal requires you to verify your identity using the third-party ID.me service before you can access your benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct control over sharing your highly sensitive personal and biometric data with a third-party verification service.

questions.question: Which multi-factor authentication method do you want to use?
questions.why: The portal requires setting up an additional layer of protection for your account and offers options like text messages, authenticator apps, or security keys.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this setup means the agent could link the authentication to its own phone or app, potentially locking you out of your government benefits account.

questions.question: Which phone number will you use, and how do you want to receive the login code?
questions.why: The portal requires a non-VOIP phone number to receive a one-time code via text or call every time you sign in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent handle this means they might use their own phone number, complicating your ability to log in independently later.

questions.question: Should you agree to share your information with the SSA and proceed without adding a second authentication method?
questions.why: The screen warns that if you lose your only authentication method, you will have to delete your account and start over.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to secure your account with a backup authentication method before proceeding.

questions.question: Do you consent to the identity verification process and its privacy terms?
questions.why: The portal requires you to agree to share your ID and personal information to verify your identity against public records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the privacy and security measures explaining how your sensitive data is protected.

questions.question: What should you do with this browser window while verifying your ID on your phone?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns you not to close the window because it will automatically load the next step once the mobile verification is complete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent cannot physically access your smartphone to take a picture of your ID, requiring you to step in and complete this out-of-band verification yourself.

questions.question: How do you proceed with the mobile identity verification?
questions.why: The screen displays an SMS from Login.gov containing both a one-time code and a document capture link, requiring a choice on how to complete the security check.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally handle the secure verification link and identity document capture sent directly to your mobile device.

questions.question: Do you need to unmask your Social Security number to verify it before submitting?
questions.why: The screen displays your Social Security number masked by default, providing a checkbox to reveal it so you can ensure it matches your records exactly before the system checks it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually confirm your sensitive identifying number is typed correctly, which could cause verification failures and delay your benefits if there is a typo.

questions.question: How do you resolve the identity verification mismatch error?
questions.why: The portal blocks access until you resolve the identity mismatch by updating your personal information with the Social Security Administration or Login.gov.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot resolve this identity mismatch because it requires updating your personal records directly with the Social Security Administration or Login.gov.

questions.question: Do you have an activation code to enter?
questions.why: The portal needs to know if you received a specific activation code via mail, text, or in person to properly verify and link your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent would not know if you previously received a specific activation code in the mail or at an office, which could delay your access.

questions.question: How do you want to receive your activation code?
questions.why: The portal requires you to choose between a text message or a phone call to receive an activation code that verifies your identity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot access the text message or phone call sent to your personal device to retrieve the required activation code.

questions.question: What is your Login.gov password to encrypt your information?
questions.why: Re-entering your password finalizes the encryption process, ensuring your sensitive data is secure and accessible only to you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Sharing your Login.gov password with an agent compromises the core security guarantee that only you can access or change your encrypted information.

questions.question: Did you actually save your personal key before confirming that you did?
questions.why: If you forget your password and do not have this key, you will be forced to verify your identity all over again.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses direct possession of their account recovery key, making them reliant on the agent to securely store and provide it to them later.

questions.question: How do you log in using your SSN and temporary PIN?
questions.why: The Claimant Login section requires your Social Security Number and the newly generated temporary PIN to access the unemployment portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user must share highly sensitive personal credentials, including their Social Security Number, with the agent to proceed.

questions.question: Which email address do you enter to log in?
questions.why: The screen requires your registered email address and a reCAPTCHA verification to initiate the login process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over which personal email address is used to access your government benefits account.

children.label: Apply for the benefit
children.note: 3.1 first - a Yes there can end the online path before it starts. 3.2 only on multi-program portals. 3.3 to 3.5 as the form asks; 3.6 per employer, repeated where the base period holds several. then 3.7; 3.8 where the state pays this way; 3.9 and 3.10 where offered, both skippable and both skipped. 6 closes it.

questions.question: Which sections of the application do I need to complete, and what is their current status?
questions.why: The application summary page lists all required categories like income, expenses, and assets, allowing you to track your progress and see what information is still needed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the high-level overview of the application's complexity and the specific categories of personal information that will be required.

questions.question: Do you want to submit an incomplete application immediately to secure your filing date?
questions.why: The popup explains that you have the right to file immediately with just your name, address, and signature to establish your application date, though it warns this might delay processing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the strategic choice to secure an earlier benefit start date by submitting a minimal application today rather than waiting until they have all their information gathered.

questions.question: How should you answer the eligibility questions regarding prior claims, recent work history, and tax withholding?
questions.why: Accurately reporting your prior unemployment claims, out-of-state work, and military service is required to determine your legal eligibility for benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your specific work history, prior claims, and tax withholding preferences are reported accurately to the state.

questions.question: How should I answer the initial eligibility questions?
questions.why: These first five questions determine if you meet the basic legal requirements to proceed with the unemployment insurance application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to ensure your specific employment circumstances are accurately represented in the critical first eligibility check.

questions.question: Which benefit programs do you want to apply for?
questions.why: The 'Pick programs' screen requires you to select specific options like SNAP, TANF, or Health Care to determine the correct application path.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong assistance program, potentially delaying or misdirecting your access to crucial benefits.

questions.question: Which health care category best describes your situation?
questions.why: The screen lists specific demographic categories like 'Pregnant women' or 'Adults caring for a child', and selecting the correct one determines your eligibility for Medicaid or CHIP.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might select a category that doesn't accurately reflect your life circumstances, potentially leading to an incorrect application or denial of benefits.

questions.question: Are you filling out this form for yourself or someone else?
questions.why: The form requires you to specify if you are applying for yourself and your household or on behalf of someone else.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally ensure the application correctly identifies whether it is for your own household or another individual.

questions.question: Do you want to designate an authorized representative to act on your behalf?
questions.why: This determines whether you want to grant another person the legal right to manage your benefits application and communicate with the agency for you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent cannot know if you have a trusted individual you want to designate to handle your benefits or if you prefer to manage them yourself.

questions.question: Which address and contact details should I provide here?
questions.why: The screen requires your residence address, an optional mailing address, phone numbers, and email to ensure the agency can reach you about your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over specifying your preferred contact methods, such as enabling text messages or choosing a separate mailing address.

questions.question: Have you verified that your personal information is correct before clicking next?
questions.why: Proceeding past this screen confirms that your contact and demographic details are accurate, which is essential for the agency to process your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally spot-check your identifying details for typos or outdated information that could delay your benefits.

questions.question: What demographic information do you want to provide?
questions.why: The screen asks for personal details like race, ethnicity, gender, and disability status, which you may prefer not to answer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice of whether to disclose or withhold sensitive demographic information.

questions.question: Are the default language settings correct, and do you need an interpreter?
questions.why: The screen asks for your preferred reading language and whether you need an interpreter, which dictates how the agency will communicate with you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to specify a non-English language preference or request an interpreter for your case.

children.label: Report the work history
children.note: 3.6.1, then 3.6.2 and 3.6.3 per employer; 3.6.4 loops back into 3.6.1 for each further base-period employer (Or9Z adds one, then flips the gate answer to No). 3.6.5 wherever a free-typed occupation is refused; 3.6.6 where the claim doubles as a job-search profile. 5.4 is this goal's reopen twin, built on the state's wage records instead.

questions.question: Did you work for an employer within the last 18 months?
questions.why: Accurately reporting your employment history over the specified timeframe is required to determine your benefit eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent might incorrectly report your recent work history, potentially resulting in a denied or delayed claim.

questions.question: Is my last employer's information completely accurate before I proceed?
questions.why: The screen displays a summary of your most recent employment details, which must be correct to prevent delays or denials in processing your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that your previous employment dates and employer contact details were entered correctly before advancing the application.

questions.question: Are your employment details, specifically the reason for separation, correct?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a reason for separation, such as 'Laid Off' or 'Discharge/Fired', which directly determines your eligibility for unemployment benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to accurately report why your employment ended, risking a denied claim or penalties if the wrong reason is selected.

questions.question: What are the details of your employment separation and did you receive any additional payments?
questions.why: The screen requires your supervisor's name, last date worked, separation reason, and any additional payments like holiday pay to accurately process your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent fill this out means losing control over the exact separation reasons and payment declarations submitted to the government on your behalf.

questions.question: How do you calculate your gross wages for each past quarter if you don't have exact pay stubs?
questions.why: The form requires you to enter gross wages for six specific past quarters, which directly impacts your benefit calculation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the estimated quarterly wages accurately reflect your actual past work hours and pay rate.

questions.question: Are the gross wages you entered consistent with your last day worked?
questions.why: Entering a full quarter's worth of wages contradicts your earlier entry showing your last day worked was weeks before the quarter ended, which could trigger a fraud flag or delay your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your reported income mathematically aligns with your actual employment dates to prevent your application from being rejected or audited.

questions.question: Did you have any regular employment outside of Ohio since October 1, 2018?
questions.why: The application requires you to list all regular out-of-state employment since October 1, 2018, excluding military or federal civilian jobs already provided.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent might omit or incorrectly report your out-of-state work history, which could delay or jeopardize your benefit claim.

questions.question: Were you provided with a Mass Layoff or Buyout Identification Number by your employer?
questions.why: This determines if your unemployment claim is tied to a specific company-wide event, which requires entering the provided ID number and confirming recent work history.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might not know if you received a specific layoff ID from your employer or if you had other recent jobs, potentially delaying your claim.

questions.question: How do you find and select the correct occupation codes for your job profile?
questions.why: Using the 'Occupation Lookup' button ensures your work history is accurately categorized with the standard codes required for the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally search the lookup tool to ensure the selected occupation code perfectly matches your specific job duties.

questions.question: Do you need to select two occupations since both fields are marked as required?
questions.why: The page instructions say to select 'up to 2 occupations', but both occupation fields have asterisks indicating they are mandatory.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might arbitrarily select a second occupation just to satisfy the form validation, potentially misrepresenting your actual job search preferences.

questions.question: How many months of experience and which specific skills should you list for your selected occupations?
questions.why: The screen requires you to input your months of experience for two specific occupation codes and describe the skills that qualify you for those roles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess your experience level or list generic skills that do not accurately reflect your actual work history and qualifications.

questions.question: What is the lowest acceptable hourly wage and shift schedule you will declare you are willing to work?
questions.why: The state uses your minimum acceptable wage and shift availability to determine if you are genuinely available for work; setting the wage too high or restricting shifts can automatically disqualify you from receiving benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess a minimum wage or shift preference that either disqualifies you for being too restrictive or legally commits you to accepting jobs you cannot actually take.

questions.question: How do you answer the eligibility questions about other income, recall dates, and school or union status?
questions.why: The screen requires details on pensions, severance pay, and recall dates, which directly determine your eligibility and benefit amount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that your specific financial details and employment status are reported accurately.

questions.question: Did you work for an educational institution during the specified timeframe?
questions.why: This matters because recent employment with an educational institution can trigger specific eligibility rules or restrictions for your benefit claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might incorrectly report your employment history, potentially leading to wrongful denial or delays in receiving benefits.

children.label: Choose how benefits arrive
children.note: 3.8.1, with 3.8.2 read where the card is chosen or is the default; 3.8.3 and 3.8.4 where the form offers them. applications only - certifications touch withholding through 4.7, and D3uH sets 3.8.4 from inside account setup.

questions.question: How would you like to receive your benefit payments?
questions.why: The portal requires you to choose between receiving your funds via direct deposit to a bank account or automatically receiving a prepaid debit card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose control over the specific financial account or method used to access your benefit funds.

questions.question: How do you want to receive your benefit payments?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose between direct deposit and a ReliaCard debit card for receiving your funds and to acknowledge the associated terms.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose your preferred payment method and personally review the terms and conditions of the prepaid debit card.

questions.question: Are you comfortable with the fees and terms associated with the debit card payment option?
questions.why: The screen displays the U.S. Bank ReliaCard fee disclosure, detailing potential costs like out-of-network ATM and inactivity fees that will affect your benefit funds.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate the debit card's fee structure and decide if another payment method might save you money.

questions.question: Do you want federal and state taxes withheld from your benefit payments?
questions.why: This determines whether taxes are deducted directly from your benefits, which affects both your immediate payout amount and your end-of-year tax liability.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent make this choice means losing control over your personal tax strategy and the net amount of your immediate benefit payments.

questions.question: Do you want taxes withheld from your payments, and how should your 1099G form be delivered?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose whether to withhold 10% for federal and state taxes, and whether to receive your 1099G tax form electronically or by mail.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over managing your immediate tax liabilities on the benefit income and your preference for receiving annual tax documents.

questions.question: How do I access my homepage after updating my preferences?
questions.why: The screen confirms your preferences were successfully updated and provides a button to continue to your my Social Security homepage.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual confirmation that your account preferences were saved correctly before entering the main portal.

questions.question: How do you want to receive notices from Social Security?
questions.why: You must choose whether to receive only secure online notices or both paper and online notices before saving and continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide whether you receive important physical mail or only digital communications from Social Security.

questions.question: Do you want to backdate this claim, and if so, to what date and for what reason?
questions.why: The system requires a specific effective date and a written explanation if you choose to backdate your unemployment claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to provide their specific personal justification for the delayed filing, which is required to process the backdate request.

questions.question: Did the application let you proceed to the next screen without filling in the required reason for backdating?
questions.why: The system advanced to the Employer screen even though the field marked with an asterisk for backdating the claim was left blank.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to ensure their application is fully complete, risking a delay or denial if the agency later flags the missing explanation.

questions.question: Should you upload more documents or proceed with submitting your application?
questions.why: The screen warns that you are about to submit and recommends uploading as many documents as possible beforehand.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide if providing additional optional documents might strengthen or speed up your specific claim.

questions.question: Which of the suggested documents do you want to upload now?
questions.why: The screen lists suggested documents like proof of income that you can upload now, though it notes you can still submit the application without them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to gather and provide these documents immediately or wait for the eligibility worker to require them.

children.label: Certify a claim week
children.note: 4.1, then 4.2 and 4.3 as the portal interposes them. 4.4, with 4.5 where a No on earnings spawns it; 4.6 as the state requires. repeat 4.4 to 4.6 once per claim week in the session - lVpW and urAf each run two. 4.7 rides on the final week only. 6 closes it.

questions.question: Are there weeks available to certify for benefits, and what is the deadline?
questions.why: The dashboard notification indicates you have weeks available to certify and warns that missing the specified deadline could affect your eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your current claim balance and the exact deadline required to keep your benefits active.

questions.question: Should you read the detailed eligibility text before clicking the 'Certify for Benefits' button?
questions.why: The screen displays detailed eligibility information below the notification box that could contain important requirements or updates for your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the specific eligibility criteria presented on the screen before initiating the certification process.

questions.question: Do you understand the weekly certification rules and want to proceed?
questions.why: The screen explains that unemployment payments are based on a Sunday through Saturday period and require a weekly certification to receive benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss reviewing the specific rules and timeframes required to maintain your unemployment benefits.

questions.question: What fraud rules must I acknowledge to proceed?
questions.why: You must check the box to confirm you understand the penalties for fraud, such as failing to report new earnings, before you can continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the specific legal obligations and fraud penalties you are being held accountable for.

questions.question: Is your contact information correct, or do you need to update it?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that you must keep your contact information current, requiring you to verify the displayed address, phone, and email before continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the agency has your most up-to-date address and phone number for critical benefit communications.

questions.question: Were you too sick or injured to work for reasons other than COVID-19?
questions.why: The form requires you to declare if a non-COVID illness or injury prevented you from working in order to determine your ongoing eligibility for benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to accurately and truthfully report your specific health status and availability for work during the claim period.

questions.question: Was there any other reason preventing you from working full-time?
questions.why: This question determines your ongoing eligibility by confirming you were available to accept full-time work during the certification period.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you risk an agent incorrectly reporting your personal availability, which could lead to denied benefits or fraud penalties.

questions.question: Did you receive any of the listed types of alternative income during this week?
questions.why: The screen requires you to clarify if you received alternative income like a pension, vacation pay, or bonus during the specified week to ensure accurate benefit calculation.
