tree.note: do 1, with 2 where the venue shows rules and windows - three keepers land straight in the forms and skip 2. then 3, and 4 where drug costs drive the choice (the four Medicare keepers). the middle by regime: 5 on the marketplace routes, 6 on the employer routes, neither on the entitlement route - the benefit is fixed and the work is proving eligibility (iPQr, BEkw). 5 reaches back into 4 and re-reads the list until the configuration settles (fB0o, 5ISG, ma8-). then 7 where an application exists - on the employer routes the elections are the application, so 6 goes straight to 8. then 8, and 9 as far as the venue lets verification run in-session.

questions.question: Do you want to learn more about your options first, or are you ready to view plans?
questions.why: The site asks if you want to learn more about Medicare options or view plans directly to determine if you need educational guidance before shopping.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent decides whether to skip the educational materials, potentially bypassing foundational information you might have wanted to review.

children.label: Reach the enrollment system
children.note: 1.1, then whichever entry the venue demands: 1.2 with 1.3 where the portal re-asks inside (mtI4), 1.4 where the login fails or the site allows it (Lwux, all four Medicare keepers), 1.5 on the captcha-only portal, 1.6 when an agent works someone else's case. then 1.7 where enrollment lives behind an event or a banner.

questions.question: Will you log in to your account or proceed as a guest to start comparing plans?
questions.why: The homepage provides options to "Find health & drug plans" directly or "Log in" to access your personal information and saved preferences.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing your secure Medicare account credentials with an agent.

questions.question: Do you need to create a new account to proceed?
questions.why: The login screen provides a "Create an account" button for users who do not yet have a secure Medicare account to save their information and compare plan costs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent will establish your secure Medicare account credentials on your behalf, which requires sharing highly sensitive personal information.

questions.question: Which search result should you click to reach the official Medicare site?
questions.why: The search results displayed several commercial ads and third-party sites before the official Medicare.gov link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify they are using the official government portal instead of a commercial broker's site.

questions.question: Is this the correct website to start your health insurance application, or did you land on an unrelated career portal?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'Career Path Germany' logo and text about international career adventures, which suggests you are not on a health insurance marketplace.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to realize they are on the wrong website and immediately redirect to the proper health insurance exchange.

questions.question: Is my username entered correctly to proceed to the password step?
questions.why: The screen shows a login page with a username field and a 'Continue' button, which must be correct to access the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify that the correct account is being accessed before proceeding.

questions.question: What are your login credentials, and do you want to save your username for next time?
questions.why: The login screen requires a username and password to access the enrollment portal and offers a checkbox to save the username for future visits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means handing over your private account credentials and losing direct control over whether they are stored on the device.

questions.question: What is the one-time password sent to your mobile number?
questions.why: The portal requires the OTP sent to your phone to verify your identity before you can proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means sharing a time-sensitive security code, which compromises your account's multi-factor authentication protections.

questions.question: Do you want to review and update the application that was started for you?
questions.why: The screen shows that a pre-filled application is available and outlines the steps and deadline to complete it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to decide whether to proceed with the pre-filled application or start a new one.

questions.question: Are you ready to start the process to renew or change your coverage?
questions.why: The portal requires you to complete all enrollment steps to secure coverage for the upcoming year, even if you just want to keep your current plan.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss seeing the exact deadlines for when you need to enroll to get specific coverage start dates.

children.label: Learn the rules and window
children.note: any of it, in any order, before the choices open - 2.4 is the one hard gate (mtI4). the marketplace keepers mostly skip this goal; the welfare keepers read 2.3 and 2.5 as static pages before applying.

questions.question: What is my default plan for next year if I don't make a change?
questions.why: The screen displays the specific 2026 plan you will default into, which is critical to identify because its premiums and benefits may change from your current coverage.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct awareness of which plan you will automatically roll over into and the reminder that its costs and coverage might change next year.

questions.question: Do you meet the specific disability eligibility criteria for the Niramaya scheme?
questions.why: The presentation explicitly lists Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, and Multiple Disabilities as the covered conditions, so you must confirm your eligibility before proceeding to the portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly navigate to the enrollment portal without verifying if your specific condition qualifies under these strict guidelines.

questions.question: Do you have the required UDID card and understand that this scheme is reimbursement-only?
questions.why: The scheme description explicitly states that coverage requires a valid disability certificate or UDID card and operates strictly on a reimbursement basis.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might enroll you in a plan you are ineligible for or commit you to upfront out-of-pocket costs you cannot afford.

questions.question: What are the rules and requirements for creating my account?
questions.why: The screen displayed a warning popup with seven specific instructions in Bengali that outline the requirements for proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to know the specific rules and obligations you are agreeing to when setting up your health insurance account.

questions.question: Do you accept the warning that your information cannot be edited after submission?
questions.why: The screen displays a notice stating that edits won't be possible after submission, requiring you to click 'I Understand & Accept' to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to personally acknowledge the strict no-edit policy before proceeding with the application.

questions.question: What steps are required to complete the online registration process?
questions.why: The screen outlines a six-step process for online registration, including document uploads and payment, which sets expectations before starting the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss the upfront overview of the specific documents and steps required to successfully apply.

questions.question: Do you want to read the salient features of the scheme?
questions.why: The 'Home' dropdown contains links to 'Eligibility' and 'Salient Features', which explain the key benefits of the program before you start the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the chance to read the program's highlights and confirm it aligns with their expectations.

children.label: Describe who needs covering
children.note: the venue's intake in its own order - 3.1 first on the agent route, where the answers exist on paper before the site is touched. 3.2 to 3.7 as asked; 3.8 where the form ends in a screening verdict (Lwux).

questions.question: What coverage year, ZIP code, and type of Medicare plan do you want to search for?
questions.why: The system needs your coverage year, ZIP code, and specific plan type—such as a Part D drug plan—to display the correct Medicare options for your area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the search is tailored to your specific location, timeline, and exact Medicare coverage needs.

questions.question: What is your ZIP code, Medicare status, date of birth, and financial help status?
questions.why: These details determine which plans are available in your specific area and whether you can fully enroll or just view options without a Medicare number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might use incorrect demographic or financial information, leading to inaccurate plan options or estimated costs.

questions.question: Which type of Medicare plan do you want to search for?
questions.why: The screen requires choosing between distinct coverage types like Medicare Advantage, Part D, or Medigap, which dictates the entire set of plans that will be displayed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide which specific category of Medicare coverage best aligns with your personal healthcare needs.

questions.question: Which type of Medicare coverage do I want to shop for, and what are my ZIP code and date of birth?
questions.why: This matters because the portal needs your specific coverage preference, like a Part D drug plan, along with your location and age to display the correct available plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent might select the wrong coverage type or enter incorrect personal details, resulting in irrelevant plan options.

questions.question: Did you select the correct coverage year and enter your accurate ZIP code?
questions.why: Choosing the right coverage year and ZIP code ensures you are viewing the correct health plans and prices available for your specific location and timeframe.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally verify that the search is targeting your exact local market for the upcoming year.

questions.question: What pincode and mobile number should you enter to view the available plans?
questions.why: The screen requires a valid pincode and mobile number before the 'VIEW PLANS' button can be used to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might enter an incorrect location or phone number, leading to inaccurate plan options or misdirected communications.

questions.question: Are my dependents listed correctly, or do I need to add anyone else?
questions.why: The screen lists your spouse and child with their details, and you must confirm this is accurate or use the 'add dependent +' link to ensure everyone who needs coverage is included.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent handle this means you lose the chance to personally verify that your family members' sensitive details, like SSNs and dates of birth, are entered correctly.

questions.question: Which family members do you want to enroll in this coverage?
questions.why: Checking or unchecking dependents instantly updates the estimated plan costs displayed on the screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the real-time visibility into exactly how adding each specific dependent changes your premium costs.

questions.question: Is your pre-filled personal information accurate and up to date?
questions.why: Verifying your pre-filled name, date of birth, and address ensures your insurance application is processed correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to catch and correct outdated personal details like your address or tobacco use status before they are submitted.

questions.question: Do you want to check if your household can save money on coverage costs?
questions.why: The application overview highlights that determining eligibility for financial assistance is a primary goal of the form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to explicitly choose whether to pursue the cost-savings evaluation path before beginning the application.

questions.question: Is this calculated monthly income accurate, and is your income hard to predict?
questions.why: The screen shows a calculated monthly income of $0.00 from your self-employment and asks if this estimate is correct or if your income is hard to predict.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to correct the system's zero-dollar estimate and accurately report your unpredictable self-employment income.

questions.question: Do you qualify for any financial assistance with your drug costs?
questions.why: The screen displays your Extra Help status for the upcoming years, indicating whether your income qualifies you for assistance with Medicare costs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss seeing your official eligibility status for financial assistance, which could drastically change how you budget for your prescriptions.

questions.question: How much of a premium tax credit do you qualify for?
questions.why: The screen displays your eligibility results and a specific tax credit amount, which directly determines your actual out-of-pocket costs when comparing plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify your exact financial assistance amount and understand how it will offset your monthly premiums.

children.label: Enter the drugs and pharmacies
children.note: runs only where drug costs drive the choice - the intake's own question opens it (4.1). 4.2 and 4.3 per drug, 4.4 where the system knows a generic, 4.5 closes each pass; repeat until the list is done. 4.7 for up to five slots. 4.6 and 4.8 are the re-entry points - 5's plan reaches back here because the estimate is conditional on this goal's outputs.

questions.question: Do you want to retrieve your saved drug list using a drug ID, or should I enter your medications manually?
questions.why: The screen provides a 'Retrieve My Saved Drug List' option to quickly load your prescriptions using a drug ID.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to securely manage your own medication list and transition it to a new Medicare account yourself.

questions.question: Should you retrieve your saved drug list using a Drug List ID or by logging into a MyMedicare account?
questions.why: The screen shows fields for a Drug List ID and Password Date, but this legacy retrieval method is becoming obsolete in favor of the MyMedicare.gov login.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that the Drug List ID system is retiring and the opportunity to personally set up a MyMedicare account to secure your medication records.

questions.question: Do you want to include your prescription drug costs in the plan comparison, and how do you usually fill them?
questions.why: Including drug costs requires entering specific medication details and pharmacy preferences to ensure the plan comparison accurately reflects your expected out-of-pocket expenses.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might skip adding your specific medications or guess your preferred pharmacy type, potentially leading to a plan with poor coverage for your actual prescriptions.

questions.question: Do you want to include your prescription drug costs in the plan comparison?
questions.why: The screen asks if you want to see your drug costs when comparing plans, which determines whether the system will calculate out-of-pocket expenses for your specific medications.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might skip entering your medications, potentially resulting in a plan choice that does not adequately cover your specific prescriptions.

questions.question: Which of your recently filled medications do you want to add to your plan comparison list?
questions.why: The screen presented a list of recently filled drugs to include for cost estimates, and selecting the right ones ensures accurate plan comparisons.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would not know which of your past medications you still take or want to factor into your future plan's cost estimates.

questions.question: Which prescription drug should you add to your list?
questions.why: Entering your specific medications allows the portal to accurately estimate your out-of-pocket costs and verify formulary coverage for the plans shown.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally ensure that all your essential daily medications are correctly factored into the plan comparison.

questions.question: Do the prepopulated dosage and quantity match your current prescription?
questions.why: Adjusting the dosage and quantity fields for your medication ensures the system calculates accurate out-of-pocket costs for your specific prescription needs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might accept the default medication values, leading to inaccurate cost estimates that do not reflect your actual prescription usage.

questions.question: What dosage, quantity, and refill frequency should you select for your prescription?
questions.why: The system defaults to a 5mg tablet and 60 pills a month, so you must adjust these to match your actual prescription to get accurate plan cost estimates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might accept the default dosage and frequency, leading to inaccurate cost estimates and potentially choosing the wrong insurance plan.

questions.question: Do you want to add the generic version of this drug to potentially save money, or keep the brand name?
questions.why: The portal offers a generic alternative that might cost less, which directly impacts the estimated out-of-pocket costs used to compare plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically select the cheaper generic option, overriding your specific medical need or preference for the brand-name medication.

questions.question: Do you want to add the generic version of your medication or keep the brand name?
questions.why: The portal suggests a generic alternative that may cost less, requiring you to choose which version to use for your plan comparison and cost estimates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether you are comfortable taking a generic medication to save money or if you strictly require the brand-name prescription.

questions.question: Is your list of saved medications complete and accurate?
questions.why: Confirming your saved drugs list, which currently includes Eliquis, Levothyroxine, and Lisinopril, ensures the plan comparison accurately reflects your real out-of-pocket costs without being skewed by hypothetical medications.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might add hypothetical medications or miss a current prescription, which would distort the estimated costs and lead to selecting a suboptimal insurance plan.

questions.question: Which drug do you want to remove from your saved list?
questions.why: The screen showed your saved drugs list, and removing a medication changes the estimated prescription costs used to compare plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide which specific medications to exclude from their coverage and cost estimates.

questions.question: What location and pharmacy name should I use to search for your preferred pharmacies?
questions.why: The screen allows you to search for up to five pharmacies by zip code and name to ensure the plans you compare cover your preferred locations.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure the plans being compared include the specific pharmacy locations that are most convenient for you.

questions.question: Which specific pharmacy location do you want to add to your profile?
questions.why: The search results display multiple CVS locations near [number], such as the ones on Whitmore Lake Rd and Challis Rd, so you must select the exact one you visit to ensure accurate prescription pricing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify your preferred local pharmacy, which could result in the agent selecting a location that is less convenient for you to visit.

questions.question: Do you need to edit your list of saved pharmacies?
questions.why: The screen displays your four currently saved pharmacies and their network status, prompting you to decide if you need to update the list before comparing plan costs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might proceed with an outdated or inconvenient pharmacy list, which could result in inaccurate out-of-pocket cost estimates for your prescriptions.

questions.question: Do you want to check if other local pharmacies offer lower estimated drug costs?
questions.why: The screen shows a significant difference between your current retail pharmacies and the preferred mail-order option, making it worth checking if other local pharmacies offer better rates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to optimize your out-of-pocket costs by comparing prices across your preferred local pharmacies.

children.note: 5.1 where filters exist - 5.1 also owns the empty-set escape (Lwux). 5.2, then 5.3 on the ranked cards; 5.4 per candidate, and most keepers walk exactly one. the loop the corpus insists on: reach back into 4.6 or 4.8, change an input, and re-read 5.3 - the ranking is not stable under the inputs (fB0o, 5ISG, ma8-).

questions.question: Do you want to review the estimated costs for your current plan before comparing new options?
questions.why: The screen displays your current Wellcare Value Script plan with its $0 premium and $30 estimated drug costs, establishing a baseline for comparison.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate whether your existing coverage is still your best option before an agent explores or selects alternatives.

questions.question: How do your new medications affect your current plan's estimated costs and coverage?
questions.why: Confirming that your current plan covers all four drugs for an estimated $30.00 provides a clear baseline before you search for alternative plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct reassurance of seeing exactly how your specific prescriptions impact your out-of-pocket costs under your current coverage.

questions.question: What minimum star rating do you want to require for the plans?
questions.why: Filtering by star rating narrows down the 27 available prescription drug plans to only those meeting your specific quality standards.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide how strictly to weigh quality ratings against having a wider variety of plans to choose from.

questions.question: Do you want to filter for plans that are accepted across the U.S.?
questions.why: Checking the "Accepted across U.S." box narrows the available options down to 18 prescription drug plans that offer national coverage.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether having nationwide pharmacy access is more important than seeing the full, unfiltered list of local plan options.

questions.question: How do you want to sort the available prescription drug plans to compare your options?
questions.why: The portal defaults to sorting the 27 available plans by lowest monthly premium, but changing the sort to lowest drug cost might better reflect your actual out-of-pocket expenses.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide which financial metric, such as monthly premium versus total drug cost, is most important for your personal budget.

questions.question: Which health insurance provider do you want to register with, TK or AOK?
questions.why: The screen presents distinct registration options for TK and AOK public insurance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to select their preferred health insurance provider for registration.

questions.question: Which plan tier best fits your preferred balance of monthly premiums and out-of-pocket costs?
questions.why: The screen explains that plan categories determine how you and the insurance company share costs, which dictates your overall financial risk.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to weigh your personal risk tolerance and budget against the general cost structures of the Bronze, Silver, and Gold tiers.

questions.question: Which specific details of this plan do you want to review before returning to the search results?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple expandable sections like benefits, costs, and star ratings that provide deeper insight into the plan.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to examine specific plan details like extra benefits or drug costs before deciding to look at other options.

questions.question: Are the details of this plan satisfactory, or should you go back to the list?
questions.why: The screen shows a monthly premium of $41.70 and estimated annual drug costs of $500.40, which you must evaluate before deciding to enroll or keep looking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent decides whether these specific premium and drug costs are acceptable for your budget.

questions.question: Should you review the specific coverage details and copays for this HMO plan?
questions.why: Opening the details modal reveals the plan summary table, which helps you understand exactly what the $155 per pay period covers for your family.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the chance to personally verify the specific copays and coverage limits that will dictate your family's out-of-pocket medical costs.

questions.question: What is the identifying information for this specific plan?
questions.why: Recording the exact plan name and Plan ID ensures you or your agent enroll in the correct Medicare Advantage plan.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might proceed with enrollment without explicitly sharing the Plan ID, leaving you without the exact reference number for your records.

questions.question: Are you satisfied with this Silver plan's costs, or should you go back to compare it with a Bronze plan?
questions.why: Evaluating the $74.68 premium, $3,700 deductible, and specific copays helps you determine if a different tier might offer a better balance of costs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally weigh the trade-offs between this plan's specific out-of-pocket costs and the potential premium savings of a Bronze plan.

questions.question: What will my total yearly cost for premiums be?
questions.why: Using a calculator to multiply the displayed monthly premium by 12 months reveals your total expected out-of-pocket cost for the year.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally calculate and internalize the full annual financial impact of the chosen plan's premiums.

questions.question: Are your selected pharmacies in-network, and are any of them preferred pharmacies that might offer lower costs?
questions.why: The screen shows CVS and Kroger as standard in-network and mail order as preferred in-network, which determines your estimated drug costs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might just verify that your local pharmacy is in-network without realizing you would be willing to use a preferred mail-order pharmacy for the extra cost savings.

questions.question: Which pharmacy offers the lowest costs for your prescriptions?
questions.why: Comparing the drug costs during coverage phases reveals that using a mail-order pharmacy reduces the cost of generics like Lisinopril to $0.00 compared to retail options like CVS or Kroger.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to weigh the convenience of your local retail pharmacies against the out-of-pocket savings of a mail-order service.

questions.question: How does the plan's deductible affect your out-of-pocket costs for each specific medication?
questions.why: Seeing that a Tier 3 drug requires paying the full $746 retail cost before the deductible is met, while Tier 1 drugs have immediate low copays, helps you accurately estimate your early out-of-pocket expenses.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct visibility into the immediate cash burden you will face at the pharmacy counter for your specific medications early in the year.

questions.question: Will you meet the deductible, and what are your estimated monthly drug costs?
questions.why: Seeing the projection that you won't meet the $415.00 deductible and have $0.00 monthly drug costs helps you accurately gauge your expected out-of-pocket expenses for this plan.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct reassurance of seeing the zero-dollar monthly breakdown and the explicit confirmation that your specific medications won't trigger the deductible.

questions.question: How do my estimated out-of-pocket drug costs change month by month across these different pharmacies?
questions.why: The screen breaks down your estimated drug costs month by month across different retail and mail-order pharmacies, revealing exactly when deductibles or refill schedules will cause your expenses to spike.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to anticipate your highest out-of-pocket months and decide whether the savings from a preferred mail-order pharmacy are worth changing your routine.

questions.question: What tiers are my medications in, and what are the specific copays, coinsurance, and quantity limits for them?
questions.why: Seeing that a specific drug like Eliquis is Tier 3 with a 20% coinsurance and quantity limits helps you accurately estimate your actual monthly out-of-pocket costs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify how your specific prescriptions are classified and whether the resulting coinsurance or quantity limits fit your budget.

questions.question: How do your copays for different drug tiers compare between preferred and standard pharmacies?
questions.why: The screen displays the specific copays and coinsurance for each drug tier, which vary depending on whether you use a preferred or standard retail pharmacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to see exactly how much more you will pay out-of-pocket if your local pharmacy is standard rather than preferred.

questions.question: How do you want to browse the list of in-network hospitals?
questions.why: The dropdown menu offers several ways to view the hospital network, including by specialty, grade, or a general empanelled list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to filter the network search by the specific medical specialties or hospital grades that matter most to your healthcare needs.

questions.question: Which specific empanelment information or tool do you want to access?
questions.why: The screen presented a 'Hospital Empanelment' dashboard with various options like 'Empanelled Hospital List' and 'Package List'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent would have to guess whether you want to view the package list, empanelled hospitals, or another specific tool.

lookup.task: look up a specific parameterized public fact and read off the right value: enter the identifying parameters (a place and day for a weather forecast on weather.com or accuweather, a flight number on flightaware or the airline's site, a route and time on a transit-schedule site, a team for a sports score, a channel for a TV listing), get the result for those parameters, and read the needed value; complete when the queried value for the RIGHT parameters (right city, right flight number, right date, right route) is on screen. Surface pinned: a public information site or app (weather, flight-status, transit-schedule, sports scores, TV listings). Variants: news commentary or analysis videos, storm-chasing/weather-event footage, sports highlight reels, and app "review" content do not belong.

mapnav.task: get directions to a specific place with an online map (Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze): search the destination, pick a travel mode, review the route options (time, tolls, transit lines), and start navigation or read off the chosen route; complete when the chosen route with its ETA is on screen or turn-by-turn navigation has begun. Surface pinned: the map product itself — not dashcam or driving footage, not travel vlogs that happen to show a map.

tree.label: Navigate to a destination
tree.note: do 1 - five keepers start in the phone's settings and two install the app first. 2 floats: before any destination when the preference is the point (zJVt, HrMd, 4AhB, mo0Q), through the per-route door from inside 4 (obk4, bQbE, kIU1, lYnD), or never. then 3, then 4 - except on desktop, where 4.1's form comes first and 3 happens inside it (7EYu, bQbE, 60tT). rework 4 until the route reads right. then one of three endings: 5 (sixteen keepers start guidance, none arrives on camera), 6 (keep or hand off the route instead - 7EYu, 60tT, ETAP, VO5N, sWXu), or nothing (bQbE, FfFy, HrMd, kIU1, PjID). 7 and 8 are excursions from the main map (PjID, QULM, aGGT); 7.5 reruns 3 and 4 offline.

children.label: Ready the device and app
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2 on a fresh install (1KTk, VO5N), with 1.3 where the store offers an update (QULM). 1.4 or 1.5 before the app ever opens - five keepers start at the OS level - and permission asks recur mid-task (5.2, 8.5). then 1.6, 1.7 where the platform asks, and 1.8 once the map is up. most keepers arrive with all of this already done and start at 1.6.

questions.question: Is this the best route for my trip, and should I start navigation?
questions.why: The map displays a 1 hour 32 minute motorcycle route avoiding tolls alongside a slower alternate, so you must confirm this path is acceptable before hitting start.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify the route's ETA, traffic conditions, and alternate paths before committing to the journey.

questions.question: Does the selected route reflect my toll and highway preferences before I start navigation?
questions.why: The screen displays an 'Avoiding highways and tolls' banner alongside multiple route times, requiring you to confirm the updated route is acceptable before hitting start.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your specific route restrictions were successfully applied before beginning the drive.

questions.question: Should you add the required vignette to the app or just proceed with driving?
questions.why: The screen showed a ticket alert warning that the route requires a vignette, requiring a choice between adding the pass or bypassing the warning.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent automatically skips the vignette warning, you might drive on a toll road without the proper pass and receive a fine.

questions.question: How should I respond to the notification and data sharing prompts to start navigation?
questions.why: The app displays a series of pop-ups regarding notifications and data sharing that must be dismissed or accepted to access the active turn-by-turn navigation screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their privacy preferences regarding app notifications and navigation data sharing.

questions.question: Do you want to keep the navigation sound on, switch to alerts only, or mute it entirely?
questions.why: The Sound menu displays options for 'Sound on', 'Sound off', and 'Alerts only' to control the level of audio guidance during the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might select an audio setting that either disrupts a quiet cabin or fails to provide the spoken directions you need.

questions.question: Do you want to inspect the route ahead for traffic and then re-center the map?
questions.why: Panning the map reveals a red section on highway '34' indicating traffic, and the 'Re-centre' button quickly snaps the view back to your current location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spatial awareness of exactly where the traffic delays are located along your journey.

questions.question: Which active trip settings, such as showing traffic on the map, do you want to enable?
questions.why: The expanded menu provides options to share your trip progress or display live traffic, which can help you stay informed during the drive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personalize your active navigation view with specific overlays like live traffic or safety features.

questions.question: Do you want to review the entire route and alternative paths before re-centering?
questions.why: Checking the overview map allows you to evaluate the full 87-mile path and the alternative route labeled 'Similar ETA' before returning to active navigation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually inspect the entire route and decide if the alternative path better suits your driving preferences.

questions.question: Which Coles location do you want to add as a stop?
questions.why: The search results displayed multiple Coles locations with varying distances and detour times to choose from.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the most convenient stop based on your personal preference for distance and detour time.

questions.question: Should you add this location as a new drive or as a stop on your current route?
questions.why: The screen shows buttons for 'New drive' and 'Add a stop', requiring a choice between replacing the existing itinerary or creating a multi-stop journey.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify whether they want to abandon their original destination or just make a detour along the way.

questions.question: Which specific map issue are you reporting?
questions.why: The screen displays a menu of map issues alongside a popup about a road closure on W 26th Ave, requiring you to categorize the problem.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately categorize the navigation error based on your personal knowledge of the route.

questions.question: Which type of incident do you want to report on the map?
questions.why: The screen displays a menu of reportable incidents like crashes, speed cameras, and congestion to warn other drivers on the route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to accurately report the specific real-world hazard you are currently seeing on the road.

questions.question: Do you want to access other apps like media or messages from the navigation dashboard?
questions.why: The driving mode dashboard displays icons for Calls, Messages, and Media, allowing you to use other phone features without leaving the navigation interface.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this to an agent means you lose the ability to seamlessly queue up your preferred media or check messages while the navigation runs.

questions.question: Do you want to answer or decline the incoming call?
questions.why: An incoming call banner with green and red buttons has appeared on the screen, requiring a choice that might interrupt your navigation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether this specific caller is important enough to speak with while you are driving.

questions.question: Do you want to authorize Waze to access your Spotify account?
questions.why: The screen displays an authorization prompt asking to connect Waze to Spotify for integrated music control.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to share your personal music streaming account data with the navigation app.

questions.question: Do you want to start playing music using the integrated Spotify widget?
questions.why: The screen displays a Spotify widget with playback controls, offering a way to manage audio without leaving the navigation view.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to decide whether and when to start your music during the drive.

questions.question: How do you proceed after reaching an intermediate stop?
questions.why: The screen shows options to rate the navigation or end the trip, requiring you to explicitly select 'Continue' to resume routing to your final destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to end the trip early at this stop or provide feedback on the navigation experience.

questions.question: Do you want to leave feedback on the navigation experience?
questions.why: The arrival screen displays a feedback prompt with smiley face icons to rate the trip before tapping 'Done'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might skip the rating or submit feedback that does not reflect your actual travel experience.

questions.question: How do you exit active navigation mode?
questions.why: Tapping the 'X' button stops the turn-by-turn guidance and returns you to the route overview screen showing the ETA and a Start button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to quickly cancel the active route if you need to change your plans or destination.

questions.question: Do you want to stop the automatic navigation?
questions.why: The screen indicates that navigation will start automatically and provides a 'Stop' button, requiring a decision on whether to begin the trip immediately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to cancel the active turn-by-turn navigation if they were just checking the route and are not actually ready to leave.

children.label: Keep or hand off the route
children.note: any one of 6.1 to 6.6, each its own ending: print on desktop (7EYu, 60tT), a note link where the app has no save-route feature (ETAP), a planned drive (VO5N), a calendar entry left uncommitted (sWXu), a send-to-phone (sWXu). 6.6 is the save that bites back - Set home and go starts navigating by itself.

questions.question: Do you want to review the step-by-step distances on the printable directions page?
questions.why: The printable directions page displays detailed step-by-step instructions alongside specific leg and total distances for the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to familiarize yourself with the specific distances of each leg before starting your journey.

questions.question: Should you add Street View images or map snippets to the printed directions for tricky turns?
questions.why: The print preview menu offers options to include a map or Street View image for individual steps, which helps familiarize the driver with important landmarks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might default to printing text-only directions, depriving you of the visual landmarks you would have included for confusing intersections.

children.label: Save the route to a note

questions.question: Are you sure the saved link to 'Arnprior' includes your intermediate stops?
questions.why: The Quick Note link only mentions the final destination, which could incorrectly suggest that the intermediate stops to Carp and Galetta were not saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might see only the final destination in the link title and mistakenly discard it to rebuild the multi-stop route from scratch.

questions.question: How do you initiate the process of scheduling a future trip?
questions.why: The menu provides a 'Planned drives' option and a 'Plan a drive' button to help you determine when to leave based on anticipated traffic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to manually plan the drive or connect your personal calendar and Facebook accounts for automatic event syncing.

questions.question: Do you see that the estimated drive time changed from 15 to 16 minutes after saving?
questions.why: The route preview showed a 15-minute drive to arrive at 5:00 PM, but the saved planned drives list displays a 16-minute drive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might just pass along the initial estimate without noticing the system updated the travel time in the final saved list.

children.label: Add the route to the calendar

questions.question: Do you want to save this planned route to your calendar?
questions.why: The screen displays the detailed transit schedule and arrival times, which can be exported to trigger helpful departure alerts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to integrate the trip into your personal schedule for automated reminders.

questions.question: Should you check the box to create a short URL for sharing this route?
questions.why: The screen displays a share pop-up with a long URL and a 'Short URL' checkbox, allowing you to customize the link format.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to share a concise version of the route link or just proceed to the schedule explorer.

questions.question: Which device or method should you choose to send the route to your phone?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Send to your phone' popup with multiple options, including specific connected devices, an email address, and a phone number for texting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might send the directions to an old device or an unchecked email address instead of the smartphone you actually have with you.

questions.question: Is this the correct location to save as your home?
questions.why: The screen shows a location pin and a 'Set home and go' button, making it important to verify the address before saving it as a permanent shortcut.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might save an inaccurate location as your home, which would permanently affect the routing for any future trips to this destination.

questions.question: Do you want to save this location to your favorites?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Favorites' menu with an 'Add new favorite' option, which lets you save frequently visited places for quicker access in the future.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might clutter your saved places with a one-time destination or miss the opportunity to save a place you visit often.

children.label: Use the maps offline
children.note: 7.1 then 7.2; 7.3 for what is already downloaded. 7.4 then 7.5 to prove the download works - PjID and QULM both stage the outage on purpose. 7.6 when the proof fails. 7.5 reruns 3 and 4 in miniature against the downloaded area.

questions.question: Do you need to access your profile settings or offline maps before starting your search?
questions.why: The profile icon in the top right corner provides access to additional app features like offline maps that could be necessary for your journey.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to proactively download offline maps or adjust account settings before navigating.

questions.question: Do you want to download a new offline map area or use one of the currently saved maps?
questions.why: The screen displays existing downloaded maps with their storage sizes and expiration dates, along with an option to select a new map area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manage your device's storage space and decide exactly which geographic areas need to be available offline.

questions.question: How large of an area do you want to download for offline use?
questions.why: Adjusting the blue bounding box changes the map coverage and increases the required storage space from 30 MB to 80 MB.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to balance the offline map coverage area against the storage space it consumes on your device.

questions.question: Do you want to download this map area for offline use and consume up to 80 MB of your storage?
questions.why: The screen displays a prompt asking to confirm the download of the selected map area, noting it will use up to 80 MB of free space.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might approve the download without knowing if you have enough device storage or cellular data to spare.

questions.question: Are you okay with the downloaded offline map taking up more storage space than initially estimated?
questions.why: The screen initially estimated the offline map would use up to 80 MB, but later showed the downloaded file taking up 108 MB.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to monitor their device storage accurately when the agent fails to notice that a download exceeded its estimated size.

questions.question: Do you want to update the downloaded map before it expires?
questions.why: The screen indicates that the downloaded map will expire on June 5, 2023, unless it is updated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to use your device's data and storage to keep this specific offline map current.

questions.question: Should you delete any existing offline maps to free up space?
questions.why: The screen displays a previously downloaded 49 MB map, and removing it can free up device storage before saving a new area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your device's storage management and the choice of which old maps to keep or discard.

questions.question: How do you simulate being offline to test the downloaded map?
questions.why: The Android quick settings panel displays active network connections like Wi-Fi that must be toggled off to ensure the app relies solely on downloaded data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the map will successfully provide directions without an active internet connection.

questions.question: Does the destination shown on the screen match the one you stated you are routing to?
questions.why: The audio claims to route to a gas station, but the screen shows a failed route to High Falls followed by a new search for Genesee Brew House.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate destination tracking if the agent relies on the spoken intent rather than noticing the actual on-screen routing failures and changes.

questions.question: Do you want to proceed with this offline route without live traffic data?
questions.why: The screen displays an offline icon and 'No traffic data', meaning the 15-minute estimate cannot account for current road conditions or delays.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to find an internet connection for live traffic updates or to delay the trip until real-time data is available.

questions.question: Since offline routing from your current location failed, what starting point should you select instead?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'No routes found in your offline maps' error, requiring you to choose a new origin within the downloaded area to successfully calculate a route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to troubleshoot offline map limitations by manually selecting an alternative starting point.

children.label: Share your live location
children.note: 8.1, then 8.2 to 8.4 in the sheet's order; 8.5 fires mid-flow when the platform demands background access; 8.6 closes the loop. QULM runs all of it; aGGT opens the sheet and backs out.

questions.question: How long do you want to share your real-time location, and who should I send it to?
questions.why: The screen provides options to set a specific duration for location sharing and lists various messaging apps and contacts to send the link to.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent decides this, it might share your live location with the wrong contact or leave it running indefinitely, compromising your privacy.

questions.question: Do you need to share your current location with someone?
questions.why: The 'Your Location' bottom sheet provides options like 'Share location' and 'Save parking' that are useful for coordinating with others.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to proactively send their exact coordinates to a friend they are coordinating with.

questions.question: Do you want to share your real-time location?
questions.why: The app offers to share your continuous location with others across Google services, which updates even when the app is not in use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally decide whether your continuous, real-time whereabouts are broadcasted to others.

questions.question: How long do you want to share your real-time location?
questions.why: The screen provides options to share your location for a set time, such as one hour, or indefinitely until turned off, which directly affects your privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strictly control the duration of your location sharing, potentially exposing your whereabouts longer than intended.

questions.question: Which app do you want to use to share the location link?
questions.why: The screen shows a sharing menu with multiple communication apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Messages to choose from.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide which specific messaging platform is used to send your location to others.

questions.question: Who should receive your live location link?
questions.why: The WhatsApp 'Select contacts' screen requires you to choose a recipient from your recent chats to send the live location link to.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to safely select your own number to test the feature without broadcasting your location to other contacts.

questions.question: Are you comfortable sharing your name, photo, and real-time location via a link, and do you want to suppress this warning in the future?
questions.why: The app explicitly warns that anyone with the generated link will be able to see your personal details and live location, requiring you to accept this privacy risk to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the privacy implications of broadcasting your live location and to decide whether to keep future warnings enabled.

questions.question: How do you open the shared live location?
questions.why: Tapping the provided Maps link in the WhatsApp chat directly opens the shared location in the map application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the seamless transition from their messaging app directly to the exact coordinates shared by their contact.

news.task: find the latest news about a specific topic (a company, a person, a sport, a technology) on a news site or aggregator (google news, apnews, reuters, bbc, espn): search for or navigate to the topic, sort by or judge recency, and open the relevant latest article; complete when a current article on the right topic is on screen. Surface pinned: news sites and aggregators. Variants: news commentary/opinion videos as the subject, and "daily news recap" videos where a person reads headlines to camera, do not belong.

tree.label: Keep up with the news
tree.note: do 1. 2 and 3 feed each other and repeat - the Feedly keepers build with 2 and then scan what accrues with 3; the Google keepers run 3 alone and keep nothing (RKSc, gyDs, xATD, vLA0), except one topic follow that reaches into 2.6 (64Vu). 4 from any list, though most lists are scanned and left - 9 stories and one video clip get opened across 14 keepers. 5 after 4 where the story is worth keeping; 4_Sv runs 5 without ever opening the story. 6 replaces 4 and 5 on the newsroom service (AE9a). 7 in the one keeper that closes the loop (v4vm).

questions.question: Should you browse your existing feeds or follow a new source to find the topic?
questions.why: The sidebar displays existing categories like 'Marketing' alongside a '+' icon to 'Follow New Sources', requiring a choice between current and new content streams.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally curate which specific news publications are added to your account.

questions.question: Should you choose one of these recent marketing articles, or add a new content source?
questions.why: The screen shows recent popular articles in the Marketing feed, but you may need to add a different topic to find the specific news you are looking for.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally decide whether the current feed is relevant enough or if a new topic needs to be added to the aggregator.

children.label: Get into the news service
children.note: 1.1 or 1.2 to arrive. 1.3 to 1.5 only where an account gates the service - three Feedly keepers start mid-session and skip all of it (4_Sv, zCA3, r9X3), and every Google keeper walks in without an account. 1.6 replaces 1.4 on the newsroom service (AE9a). 1.7 where the edition matters (gyDs).

questions.question: What initial platform and search context do you want to start with?
questions.why: The screen shows the Google News Timeline labs page pre-loaded with a search for 'christmas' and dates from December 2009.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to define the specific starting platform, search term, and historical timeframe for the task.

questions.question: Which search result is the official Feedly website?
questions.why: The first search result displays the URL 'https://feedly.com/', confirming it is the legitimate aggregator rather than a third-party or sponsored link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the search result URL to ensure you are accessing the authentic news platform.

children.label: Choose log in or sign up

questions.question: Do you want to log in to an existing account or create a new one?
questions.why: The homepage displays both 'GET STARTED FOR FREE' and 'LOGIN' buttons, requiring a choice based on whether you already have an account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the agent uses your existing account with its pre-configured news feeds rather than starting from scratch.

questions.question: Should you get started for free or import an OPML file?
questions.why: The screen presents options to either start a new free account or import an existing OPML file to set up your news feeds.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might create a new blank account instead of importing your existing curated news feeds.

questions.question: Which authentication method do you want to use to log in?
questions.why: The login modal presents multiple options like Google, Feedly, and various social accounts, requiring you to choose the one linked to your existing profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which personal or third-party account is used to authenticate and access their personalized news feeds.

questions.question: Which Google account should you use to sign in to Feedly?
questions.why: The screen presents multiple Google accounts to continue to Feedly, and the choice determines which personalized news feed and subscriptions are accessed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control which specific personal or work profile is associated with your news reading activity.

questions.question: Should you use the auto-filled credentials to sign in without checking the 'Remember me' box?
questions.why: The screen displays a login panel with a pre-filled username and obscured password, requiring a decision on whether to proceed and if the session should be saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to manage their own login credentials and decide whether the session should be persistently saved on the device.

questions.question: Do you need to adjust the language and region settings for your news feed?
questions.why: The sidebar currently displays 'English (Nigeria)', which will heavily influence the geographic focus and relevance of the news results you receive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify the exact cultural and geographic context that determines which local or regional news stories are prioritized.

children.label: Build the source feed
children.note: 2.1, then 2.2 or 2.3 raises candidates; 2.4 on every card, 2.5 where a sneak peek is wanted. 2.6 commits and 2.7 follows immediately - the platform will not let a follow float unfiled (2o_3); 64Vu's topic star is the exception, a follow with no filing step. 2.8 inside 2.7 when the feed is new; v4vm also runs 2.8 standalone and fills the empty feed afterward. repeat 2.2 to 2.7 per source - four in about 15 seconds (zCA3), six in a sitting (1HW8). 2.9 after any batch; 2.10 wherever the counts are on screen.

questions.question: Which source should you follow next, and which feed should you add it to?
questions.why: The search results display multiple sources like MediaShift, and selecting the right one to follow and add to your Journalism feed ensures you track the correct topic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the personal curation of deciding exactly which publications are trustworthy or relevant enough to include in your specific news feeds.

questions.question: Should you check the Explore tab to find trending articles?
questions.why: The screen displays 'Me' and 'Explore' tabs, offering a choice between personalized news and broader trending topics.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally decide whether to browse general trends or stick to your customized news feed.

questions.question: Which method should I use to add new content to your Feedly account?
questions.why: The screen presents multiple options for adding content, such as 'Publications & Blogs' or 'Keyword Alerts', which determine how the topic will be sourced.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to choose their preferred method for tracking and organizing the new topic in their feed.

children.label: Search for a topic or source

questions.question: Which language do you want to use for the search results?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Results language' dropdown with multiple options, allowing you to filter the news articles by languages like English, Spanish, or Japanese.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify your preferred reading language or to intentionally seek out foreign-language coverage of the topic.

questions.question: What specific blog or source do you want to search for?
questions.why: The search bar requires you to input the exact name of the publication or topic you want to read about.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally select a trusted, niche source that aligns with your specific professional interests.

questions.question: Which topic category should you explore to find relevant news?
questions.why: The screen displays various featured industries and skills, making it necessary to choose the right category to surface relevant news sources.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the opportunity to browse and select a specific niche topic that perfectly aligns with your current interests.

questions.question: Which regional or topical video channel should you filter by?
questions.why: The left sidebar lists multiple regional and topical video channels under Broadcast Video, requiring a choice to narrow down the news content.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to prioritize which specific region's news is most relevant to your current interests.

questions.question: Which source should you select from the matching results?
questions.why: The screen displayed multiple matching sources with varying follower counts and posting frequencies, requiring a subjective choice.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to apply their personal taste or specific niche interest when choosing among multiple valid sources.

questions.question: Which specific blog should you add from this category?
questions.why: The screen displays several business blogs with varying reader counts and article frequencies, requiring a choice of which specific perspective to follow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to select a source based on their personal appreciation for a specific author's industry reputation and writing style.

questions.question: Do the recent articles in this preview pane look relevant and interesting enough to follow?
questions.why: Scanning the article titles grouped under 'TODAY' and 'YESTERDAY' helps you verify if the source consistently publishes content that matches your target topic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally evaluate the nuance and quality of the article titles to decide if the source truly aligns with your specific interests.

questions.question: Should you follow the 'Apple' topic, or proceed directly to reading the latest articles?
questions.why: The search results page provides options to follow the overarching 'Apple' topic, browse sub-topics like 'Apple Watch', or immediately click on recent news articles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personalize your news feed by choosing which specific topics to follow for future updates.

questions.question: Do you want to follow this topic for future updates?
questions.why: Clicking the star icon changes the status to 'Following' and triggers a confirmation toast, altering your account's saved preferences.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over the curation of their personalized news feed if the agent autonomously follows topics.

questions.question: Should you add this newly followed source to an existing custom feed or create a new one?
questions.why: The dropdown menu after clicking follow requires choosing whether to organize this source into an existing category like 'Journalism' or to create a brand new feed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally organize your news sources into custom categories that match your specific reading habits.

questions.question: Which feed category should you add this source to?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple existing categories like Journalism and Photography alongside an option to create a new feed, requiring you to choose how to organize this specific source.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally curate and organize your news sources according to your own preferred mental model.

questions.question: What should you name this new feed?
questions.why: The screen provides an input field and suggestions like '+ Black women', requiring a decision on how to label the topic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to organize and name your news sources according to your own personal categories.

questions.question: Should you create a new feed category to track this topic?
questions.why: The left sidebar displays a 'Create New Feed' option, which dictates how the news topic will be organized and saved in your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally name and organize the feed category to match your specific reading preferences.

questions.question: Did the new feed appear in the sidebar, and which source should you select to view its articles?
questions.why: The sidebar updated to show 'EdTech' and 'MindShift' under 'FEEDS', confirming the topic was added and providing a way to access its articles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to confirm the feed was added successfully and to choose exactly which source to view.

questions.question: Does the feed's unread count update correctly when you add new sources?
questions.why: Seeing the unread count immediately jump to 20 confirms that the platform successfully pulled in the latest articles from the sources you just added.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual reassurance that your custom feed is correctly aggregating the specific sources you care about.

children.label: Check the counts against the earlier screens

questions.question: Do you notice the inconsistency in how unread articles are reported across different feeds?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'Black Women in History' feed claiming you are caught up despite containing an article from yesterday, while the 'Journalism' feed immediately displays accurate unread counts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might trust the false 'caught up' message and fail to find the latest news, whereas a human would manually check the feed to verify.

questions.question: Does the publication frequency shown on the feed header agree with the search result?
questions.why: The feed header for MindShift states it publishes one article per month, contradicting the search result which claimed four articles per week.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might miss this contradiction and rely on inaccurate search results regarding how often the source publishes.

children.label: Pull up the stories
children.note: 3.1 or 3.2 or 3.3 raises a list - the Google keepers pull per section or query and keep nothing, the Feedly keepers open what 2 built. 3.4 only where the surface offers filters, and vLA0 round-trips every one before a single range sticks. 3.5 on every list; 3.6 where the surface clusters outlets; 3.7 on the newsroom service. re-entered per query - three searches in a row (64Vu).

questions.question: Should you apply mute filters to hide unwanted topics from your feed?
questions.why: The screen offers a 'GET MUTE FILTERS' button designed to remove irrelevant articles and fine-tune the news feed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to permanently customize their feed by filtering out specific unwanted keywords.

questions.question: Should you add more keywords to narrow the results, or use the built-in filter tools?
questions.why: The search results for 'Red sox curse' are broad, and choosing between typing additional keywords or clicking the 'Tools' button determines how efficiently you can filter for the most recent articles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to apply your knowledge of platform-specific features to efficiently filter results instead of relying on trial-and-error keyword searches.

questions.question: Which personalized feed should you select from the sidebar to find your topic?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to bypass generic suggestions and intuitively refine the search query to match their exact, unlisted interest.

questions.question: Are you still on the 'News' tab for your search results?

questions.question: Should you keep the chronological sorting or revert to relevance?

questions.question: Did your filter restrict the search results to only show blog posts?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to notice that a filter is returning outdated blog content instead of actual news and decide to revert it.

questions.question: How far back do you want to restrict the search results?
questions.why: The dropdown offers multiple time frames like 'Past hour' or 'Past month', which determines how recent the news articles must be to appear in your results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might pick a time frame that is too broad or too narrow for your specific information needs.

questions.question: Did the filter successfully return older articles?
questions.why: Seeing older dates like 2017 and 2013 on the search results confirms that the archive filter is functioning correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation that the platform's date filters are actually working as intended before selecting an article.

questions.question: How do you specify an exact date range for the search?
questions.why: Choosing the custom range option in the date filter dropdown lets you pinpoint articles from a specific timeframe instead of relying on general archive categories.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually define the exact start and end dates that perfectly capture the specific timeframe you care about.

questions.question: Does the applied date filter accurately reflect the years you entered?
questions.why: Verifying that the system expanded your input of '1990' and '1999' to the full calendar years ensures your search covers the entire intended timeframe.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify that the system's automatic date formatting perfectly aligns with their intended search boundaries.

questions.why: The '...' dropdown menu displays both harmless sorting options like 'Latest' and the destructive 'Delete' option, requiring careful selection.

patientportal.task: use a patient portal (MyChart, FollowMyHealth, LabCorp or Quest portals, a health system's own portal): sign in and complete one concrete arc — view test results, read or send a message to the care team, view or download a visit summary or medical record, or check in for an upcoming visit; complete when the result, message, or record is on screen. Surface pinned: the portal itself — not symptom research (healthinfo), not appointment booking (doctor), not pharmacy refills (refill).

tree.label: Use the patient portal
tree.note: do 1 - 1.2 once, on a first invitation (L1Mf); 1.3 thereafter. then 2, and from 2 whichever of 3 to 6 the day's task is - each keeper walks one to three, none walks all four. 7 after any commit: 3.13, 5.9, 5.10.4, and 6.5 all hand into it. 4 gates on 3 at some clinics (CkVD: eCheck-In must complete before joining) and not others (fW6G: abandoned with Finish later, and the visit proceeds). 8 as needed and at the end.

ride.task: get a ride with a rideshare app (Uber, Lyft; paratransit and access services count as sites): set pickup and destination, compare ride options and price, request, get matched with a driver, track the approach on the map, and verify the car and driver at pickup; complete when the ride is in progress or finished with the fare screen — at minimum, the matched-driver tracking screen after the request commits. socialpost.task: publish a post to social media (Instagram, X, Facebook, TikTok): compose the post — text, photo, or clip — add caption and tags, preview how it will look to the audience, publish, and verify it is live; complete when the published post is visible on the profile or feed. Surface pinned: a social platform's posting flow on app or web. Variants: direct messages, editing the video/photo content itself, and growth or algorithm advice do not belong.

questions.question: What type of content or detail do you want to add to your post?
questions.why: The screen displays an expanded menu with options like 'Photo/video', 'Tag people', and 'Feeling/activity', requiring a decision on how to build the post.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing creative control over which specific media, tags, or activities are used to express your message.

questions.question: What caption and additional details should you include before sharing?
questions.why: The screen provides options to write a caption, add music, tag people, or include a location, all of which determine how the audience discovers and interacts with your post.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing your personal voice in the caption and the strategic choice of which tags, locations, or music best complement your content.

questions.question: What text do you want to write for the post?
questions.why: The screen displays an active text input area and keyboard, prompting you to decide on the exact message to share.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing your personal voice and the ability to craft the specific message you want to communicate to your followers.

questions.question: Should you type text into the field despite the warning to remove media?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning stating that media must be removed to use the text feature, which could falsely deter you from entering a caption.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the human intuition to test the input field and discover that the warning is a false alarm for standard text entry.

questions.question: Should you apply a visual background to your text post?
questions.why: The screen displays a row of colored and patterned background shortcuts above the keyboard, offering a way to make a simple text post more visually prominent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the creative control to preview and select a specific visual style that best matches the mood of your message.

questions.question: Which background color do you want to apply to the text post?
questions.why: The screen displays a row of color swatches that instantly update the post preview on the right, determining the visual style of the post.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the creative control to choose a background color that matches your personal brand or the mood of the message.

questions.question: Which friends do you want to tag in the post?
questions.why: The 'Tag people' screen provides a search bar and a list of suggestions to let you specify exactly who is featured in or relevant to the post.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the personal judgment of deciding which specific friends or acquaintances should be publicly associated with this content.

questions.question: Which feeling or activity do you want to attach to this post?

questions.question: Do you want to add a location to your post before tapping Post?

questions.question: Is the location you want to tag available in the suggested list?

questions.question: Which GIF should you add to your post?

questions.question: How long do you want the poll to remain active?
