stock.task: buy a specific amount of a stock or crypto in a retail app (Robinhood, Coinbase, Fidelity, Cash App): search the ticker, enter a dollar amount or share count, review the order (price, fees), place it, and see the filled or pending confirmation; complete when the order confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: a retail brokerage or crypto app or website. Variants: trading-strategy and technical-analysis content, price-prediction videos, and day-trading courses do not belong.

tree.label: Trade on an investing app
tree.note: do 1. 2 fires wherever the platform puts the wall: before the first buy (yeKU), inside the first buy (Wopd), only at send (DZKH), once per ramp even twice in one session (lBbZ). 3.1 every session; the rest of 3 as the rails demand. repeat 4 until an asset settles - 4.8 ends an orbit without a trade. then 5 and 6 as a pair, once per trade: four keepers run the pair twice, buy then sell (DZKH, eVJg, ZWfJ, lBbZ), and ten keepers run 5 without ever reaching 5.11. 7 when the holdings leave the platform (O1Ka, fDjD, lBbZ). 8 and 9 stand apart from any single trade and take over whole stretches of a session (w-mD, jH1r).

children.label: Get into the platform
children.note: 1.1 then 1.7 - most keepers arrive signed in and 1.2 to 1.6 never fire. 1.2 to 1.5 on a first run (yeKU walks all of it; frXh chooses among managed tiers first). 1.6 recurs when a session lapses mid-task (yeKU signs back in after the 3-day wait). 1.8 swaps the whole session onto simulated money (JAFQ).

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to ensure the agent clicks the authentic brokerage link rather than a deceptive ad or phishing site.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally weigh the financial risk of locking these funds into a retirement account with strict early withdrawal penalties.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to decide whether your funds are placed in a self-directed account or a robo-advisor managed account like Fidelity Go.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires giving an agent access to your personal email inbox, which exposes your private communications and other accounts.

questions.question: Do you agree to the user agreement and its stated financial risks?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the agent is navigating to the correct asset class before initiating the purchase.

Surface pinned: the web interface of a tax-filing service. Variants: checking refund status afterwards, filing through a human accountant, and standalone refund-estimator calculators do not belong.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you might miss the crucial instruction that your tickets won't be emailed and require logging into your account at the venue.

questions.question: Are your contact details already pre-filled on the checkout pages?
questions.why: The screen shows the contact details section is visibly pre-filled on both the confirmation and payment pages, confirming the advice to set this up in advance to save time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind of verifying that their tickets will be sent to the correct, pre-configured email address and phone number.

questions.question: What delivery address should I use, and are you okay with the final total including fees?
questions.why: The checkout page requires a full delivery address and displays a final total of $47.50, which includes $9.70 in service fees and $1.80 in taxes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to verify where the tickets are being sent and to decide if the added service fees make the tickets too expensive.

questions.question: Should you add ticket insurance or event extras to your order?
questions.why: The checkout screen presents optional add-ons like a reserved table upgrade and ticket insurance that will increase the final price.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to weigh the cost of insurance against your personal need for purchase protection.

questions.question: Are the final order details correct, and do you want to purchase ticket insurance before selecting a payment method?
questions.why: The checkout screen requires a decision on ticket insurance and agreement to the terms before you can enter payment details and place the order.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to review the final cost breakdown and decide if you want the protection of ticket insurance.

questions.question: Which accepted credit card will you use to pay the PHP8,025.00 total?
questions.why: The checkout screen requires specific payment details for accepted methods like Visa or Mastercard to successfully process the PHP8,025.00 charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing sensitive credit card details with the agent and losing control over which account is charged.

questions.question: Which payment method do you want to use?
questions.why: The checkout screen offers several payment options like credit card, PayPal, Klarna, and Venmo, which determine how the purchase is funded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose control over which specific financial account or financing service is charged for the tickets.

questions.question: Are you ready to accept the final total including fees and provide your card's security code to complete the purchase?
questions.why: The screen shows a final total of $175.47 that includes unexpanded fees, and requires a CVV code for the selected Mastercard before the order can be processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to review the exact fee breakdown before committing your money and the ability to ensure the payment goes through successfully by providing the required security code.

questions.question: Do you want to uncheck the default marketing and data-saving boxes before completing the purchase?
questions.why: The checkout page includes pre-checked boxes that will subscribe you to promotional emails and save your booking details if you do not actively opt out.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent leaves these boxes checked by default, you lose control over your inbox and data privacy preferences.

questions.question: Are you comfortable with the final total including the added fees, and ready to agree to the terms of use?
questions.why: The screen reveals a $47.36 service fee and a $2.95 processing fee added to the base ticket price, requiring your explicit agreement to the terms before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate if the nearly $50 in extra fees makes the final price too expensive to justify the purchase.

questions.question: Are you willing to accept the non-refundable terms to finalize this purchase?
questions.why: The checkout screen requires explicit agreement to a policy stating the tickets are non-refundable and non-exchangeable before the purchase button can be clicked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally review and accept the strict no-refund policy before their funds are permanently committed.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally verify the final price and seat details before handing over your sensitive billing information.

questions.question: Are you okay with the $30.10 service fee bringing your final total to $87.10?
questions.why: The checkout screen reveals a $30.10 service fee that significantly increases the base ticket price of $54.00.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to abandon the purchase if you feel the added service fees are too high.

questions.question: Does the processing fee in the order summary match the warning shown earlier?
questions.why: Checking that the CA $6.50 processing fee in the order summary matches the earlier info panel ensures you are not being overcharged.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the platform's final processing fees align with their upfront disclosures.

questions.question: Are you willing to pay the extra $147.64 in fees that appeared at checkout?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to decide if the final price with added fees exceeds their budget for the event.

questions.question: What is the estimated cost of this order in my local currency?
questions.why: The screen showed a calculator multiplying the 69.21 order total by an exchange rate of 1.3 to estimate the final charge in Canadian dollars.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to evaluate the converted price in their own currency to decide if the tickets are still worth buying.

questions.question: Are you ready to accept the $1,126.64 total and place your order?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Place Order' button attempts to process the payment and commits you to a $1,126.64 charge for the Las Vegas event.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to verify the exact total cost and event details before authorizing a large payment.

questions.question: Why did your order submission fail?
questions.why: A red error message stating 'Please enter valid code' appeared under the CVV field, indicating that the purchase cannot proceed without the correct security code.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the tickets you selected because the agent failed to provide the required payment security details to complete the transaction.

questions.question: How should you handle the checkout processing error?
questions.why: The screen shows an 'unable to process your request' error with a 'Return to Event Page' button, forcing you to decide how to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose your reserved tickets and get sent back to the queue if the agent clicks the return button instead of trying to preserve the session.

questions.question: Are you ready to enter your credit card details and commit to the final total before the timer expires?
questions.why: The screen displays the final total of PHP 3,050.00 and requires your payment details within a strict time limit to secure the tickets.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the final veto power over the actual charge to your credit card.

questions.question: Which specific payment details do you need to enter into the payment gateway?
questions.why: The screen displays a third-party payment gateway requiring your credit card number, expiration date, CVV, name, and email to process the final charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific credit card to use and to personally secure your financial information on a third-party site.
